results.title: d-separation and backdoor criterion | Causal Inference Class Notes
results.content: D-separation and the backdoor criterion are key concepts in causal inference using DAGs. They allow us to determine conditional independence relationships and identify sets of variables that, when adjusted for, enable unbiased estimation of causal effects from observational data. * The backdoor criterion is a graphical criterion for determining whether a set of variables is sufficient for adjusting for confounding in a causal effect estimation. * Adjusting for a sufficient set of variables that blocks all backdoor paths can eliminate confounding and enable unbiased estimation of the causal effect. * Proper adjustment for confounders requires careful selection of variables based on the causal DAG and the backdoor criterion. * If there exists a set of variables that satisfies the backdoor criterion, then the causal effect can be identified by adjusting for that set. * Epidemiological studies often use DAGs and the backdoor criterion to identify potential confounders and select adjustment variables (e.g., in studies of the effect of smoking on lung cancer, adjusting for age and sex).
